body_text:
The rational numbers are dense in the real numbers: if $x<y$,
there exists $q\in\mathbb{Q}$ with $x<q<y$. The irrational numbers
are also dense. Density says that every nonempty open interval
meets each subset; it does not say that the subsets have equal
cardinality or measure.
